c.tagline: A fortress republic of towers crowning Monte Titano.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis operate on fixed zone-based rates rather than meters; agree on the fare (or confirm the posted tariff) before departing, especially for airport/station transfers.

emergency.note: San Marino shares its telephone/emergency network structure with Italy; 113 reaches the state police (Gendarmeria/Polizia Civile) and 118 dispatches ambulance services.

hood_landmark.Borgo Maggiore: Borgo Maggiore funicular station, San Marino

hood_desc: The walled medieval capital atop Monte Titano, with the three towers, cobbled lanes and sweeping views; best for first-time visitors who want to sleep steps from the sights, though it goes quiet once day-trippers leave.

A lively market town at the foot of the cable car with everyday shops, cafes and an easy funicular ride up to the historic center; good value for travelers who want local atmosphere without the tourist premium.
San Marino's largest, most modern town near the Italian border, with supermarkets, restaurants and easy road access; suits longer stays, business travelers and anyone with a rental car.
A compact border district built around outlet shopping and duty-free stores, convenient for drivers arriving from Rimini; practical rather than scenic.
A quiet residential district near the shopping outlets offering budget-friendly stays with bus links into the capital; suited to travelers prioritizing price over location.

water.note: Well-monitored supply that's safe to drink, with EU-equivalent quality standards.

sys.n: San Marino Cableway (Funivia San Marino-Borgo Maggiore)

transit.pay: Cable car tickets are bought at the station kiosk or vending machine and can be one-way, round-trip, or combined with bus fares; local AASS buses are paid in cash on board or via prepaid tickets from tobacconists/kiosks. Contactless/card payment is limited, so carrying small euro coins and notes is recommended.
transit.hours: Cableway runs roughly 08:00-18:00/20:00 depending on season (closed some winter days); buses run daytime hours only, with very limited or no service late at night - taxis are the main after-hours option.
transit.note: San Marino has no rail network of its own; the historic Rimini-San Marino electric tramway closed in 1944, though a small preserved section runs as a heritage line near Valdragone.

train: No domestic rail; nearest station is Rimini (Italy), connected onward by bus

transit.m: Shuttle bus/private transfer to San Marino (~40 min)
Train Rimini station + local bus to San Marino (~50 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory as in Italy; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but rarely expected.
